land.soil_build.plain: How limited the soil is for houses without basements: few limits, some limits that design can solve, or severe limits that are costly or hard to solve.
land.soil_build.plain_es: Qué tan limitado es el suelo para casas sin sótano: pocas limitaciones, algunas que se resuelven con diseño o limitaciones serias, costosas o difíciles de resolver.
land.soil_build.definition: NRCS's interpretation 'ENG - Dwellings W/O Basements' (cointerp), by dominant condition: the rating that covers the largest share of the unit's rated components. It weighs slope, shrink-swell, depth to rock, flooding, wetness and other soil limits.
land.soil_build.method: soils.py adds up the share of the unit's components in each rating and keeps the largest.
land.soil_build.how_to_read: Severe limits do not mean that a house cannot be built: they mean that it needs special design, costly work or a site study.
caveats: Planning scale: the value belongs to the typical soil of the map unit, not to a single lot; it does not replace a study of the site.

land.soil_main_component.plain: The soil the layer describes for each map unit, and how much of the unit it covers.

land.soil_main_component.definition: comp is the name of the component the layer describes (a soil series, or a land type such as Urban land or Rock outcrop), cokey its SSURGO key and share the percent of the map unit it makes up (the representative value, comppct_r). It is the component with the largest share, except in a complex led by a land type with no soil (Urban land, Rock outcrop), where it is the largest classified soil when that soil makes up at least 15% of the unit.
land.soil_main_component.method: soils.py reads every component of the unit from SSURGO's component table and keeps the largest; MIN_SHARE (15%) sets when a classified soil under a land type is described instead.
land.soil_main_component.how_to_read: A share of 100 means the unit is one soil; a lower share means other soils, not described here, make up the rest.
caveats: Planning scale: the value belongs to the typical soil of the map unit, not to a single lot; it does not replace a study of the site.

land.soil_flood.plain: Whether the soil shows that it floods, often or at times, or stays wet; and, under Urban land alone, whether the ground below is river, swamp or beach deposits.
land.soil_flood.plain_es: Si el suelo muestra que se inunda, con frecuencia o a veces, o que se encharca; y, bajo terreno urbano solo, si debajo hay depósitos de río, ciénaga o playa.
land.soil_flood.definition: The most frequent monthly flooding class of the soil described (comonth.flodfreqcl): frequent or very frequent is 'floods often', occasional or rare is 'floods at times'; where it does not flood, a poorly drained soil (component.drainagecl) is 'stays wet'. In a land type with no soil (salt flats, tidal swamps) the worst class of its components; in a map unit of Urban land alone, the USGS geologic map at 1:100,000: geo_wet on young river, swamp or beach deposits, with geo naming the map unit (Qa alluvium, Qs swamp deposits, Qb beach deposits), and geo_dry on rock or older terraces.
land.soil_flood.method: soils.py reads the monthly flooding of every component (comonth) and keeps the most frequent class; the geologic outlines come from the three ArcInfo sheets of Open-File Report 98-38, read with pyogrio.
land.soil_flood.how_to_read: It complements the FEMA flood zones (hazards.flood_zones_layer), which are the official ones. A soil that floods often near a river with no FEMA zone is a place to look at more closely.
caveats: The soil records past flooding; it is not a flood zone and gives no chance of flooding in a year.
The geologic map is from 1998 and does not cover Vieques or Culebra.
Planning scale: the value belongs to the typical soil of the map unit, not to a single lot; it does not replace a study of the site.

land.soil_unit.plain: The soil map unit an area belongs to: its NRCS key, its short symbol and its name in English and in Spanish.
land.soil_unit.plain_es: La unidad del mapa de suelos a la que pertenece un área: su clave del NRCS, su símbolo corto y su nombre en inglés y en español.
land.soil_unit.definition: mukey is NRCS's key of the map unit in SSURGO; musym is the symbol printed on the soil survey's maps (for example LcF2). name is NRCS's name of the unit: the main soil series, the texture of its surface layer and its slope and other phases (for example, Lirios clay loam, 40 to 60 percent slopes). name_es is the same name in Spanish: the series is kept (it is a name) and the texture (USDA texture classes) and the phases are translated (for example, Lirios: franco arcilloso, pendientes de 40 a 60 %). A complex or an association names two or more soils that are mapped together.
land.soil_unit.method: Copied from SSURGO's mapunit table. name_es is made by soils.py (spanish()) from a table of texture classes, land types and phases; the series names are left as they are.
land.soil_unit.how_to_read: Use mukey to look the unit up in Web Soil Survey or Soil Data Access. Read the name as series, texture and slope: the same series with another texture or slope is another unit.
caveats: The Spanish name is the observatory's translation, not an NRCS name.
Planning scale: the value belongs to the typical soil of the map unit, not to a single lot; it does not replace a study of the site.

land.soil_order.plain: The most general class of the soil in US Soil Taxonomy, such as Ultisols (weathered, acid clays) or Mollisols (dark, fertile topsoil).
land.soil_order.plain_es: La clase más general del suelo en la Taxonomía de Suelos de EE. UU., como Ultisoles (arcillas ácidas y meteorizadas) o Molisoles (capa superior oscura y fértil).
land.soil_order.definition: The soil order of the main soil described (component.taxorder in SSURGO), the highest of the six levels of US Soil Taxonomy. Empty for land types with no soil (Urban land alone, rock, water).
land.soil_order.method: Copied from SSURGO's component table for the main soil described.
land.soil_order.how_to_read: Use it for the broad pattern: young soils of rivers and coasts (Entisols, Inceptisols), old weathered soils of the uplands (Ultisols, Oxisols), clays that swell and crack (Vertisols). The pop-up gives a short meaning of each.
caveats: Planning scale: the value belongs to the typical soil of the map unit, not to a single lot; it does not replace a study of the site.

land.soils_layer.plain: The soils of Puerto Rico from the soil survey of the US Department of Agriculture, shown as a map. For each area it gives the type of soil, what it formed from, how steep it is, its chemistry, and plain answers on flooding, farming and building houses.
land.soils_layer.plain_es: Los suelos de Puerto Rico según el estudio de suelos del Departamento de Agricultura de EE. UU., en un mapa. Para cada área da el tipo de suelo, de qué se formó, qué tan empinada es, su química y respuestas sencillas sobre inundación, siembra y construcción de casas.
land.soils_layer.definition: The file soils.geojson holds 802 polygon features, one or more for each soil map unit of the Soil Survey Geographic Database (SSURGO) of the USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) for Puerto Rico, Vieques, Culebra and Mona. A map unit is named after its main soil series, the texture of its surface layer and its slope phase (for example, Mucara clay, 40 to 60 percent slopes); the name is also given in Spanish (name_es), with the series kept and the texture and phases translated. For the main soil of each unit the file keeps the soil order of US Soil Taxonomy (order), the kind of material it formed in (origin, pm, pm_rock), the representative slope and its range (slope, slope_l, slope_h), and the chemistry of the top 30 cm (ph, om, ec, caco3). Three answers come from NRCS interpretations: farmland class (farm), limits for dwellings without basements (build) and flooding or wetness (flood).
land.soils_layer.method: soils.py queries Soil Data Access (keyless SQL) for the map unit polygons, components, horizons, parent material, monthly flooding, farmland class and the NRCS rating 'ENG - Dwellings W/O Basements'. The main soil is the component with the largest share of the unit; in an Urban land-<soil> complex it is the largest classified soil when it covers at least 15% of the unit, and cover names the Urban land on top with its share. Chemistry is the thickness-weighted mean of the horizons in the top 30 cm. Flooding is the most frequent monthly class of the soil described, and its drainage where it does not flood. Building limits are the rating that covers the largest share of the unit's rated components. Where the survey maps only Urban land, the USGS geologic map at 1:100,000 (Bawiec, 1998) splits it into land on young river, swamp or beach deposits (geo_wet, can flood) and land on rock or older terraces (geo_dry); Vieques and Culebra are not on that map and stay unrated. Polygons are simplified to about 10 m.
land.soils_layer.how_to_read: Choose what to show in the layer's menu: the soil type and what it formed from, the slope, the chemistry of the top 30 cm, or one of three questions (signs of flooding, farming, building houses). Untick a row of the legend to hide that class. Read it as the typical soil of an area for planning; the official flood zones are FEMA's, and this layer complements them.
caveats: A map unit names its typical soil; other soils, up to a large share of the unit (see share), sit inside it. Do not use it to decide what is under a single lot.
NRCS ratings are made at the scale of the survey and do not replace a study of the site by a licensed professional.
The flooding answer is the soil's own record of flooding and wetness, not a flood zone. The official flood zones are the FEMA ones (hazards.flood_zones_layer).
Under Urban land alone the answer comes from a geologic map at 1:100,000 made in 1998, not from the soil survey: it says what kind of ground the neighbourhood stands on, not how often it floods.
Water, quarries, landfills, made land and areas NRCS marks as not public information have no soil described and are shown as not rated.

land.soil_origin.definition: pm is the kind of parent material of the main soil as SSURGO names it (copm.pmkind: Residuum, Alluvium, Colluvium, Marine deposits ...) and pm_rock the rock or deposit it came from (copm.pmorigin: Volcanic rock, Limestone ...). origin groups pm in six classes the map draws.

land.contours_layer.plain: Lines that join points of the same height, drawn in the browser from the terrain tiles of the 3D view; closer lines as you zoom in.
land.contours_layer.plain_es: Líneas que unen puntos de la misma altura, trazadas en el navegador a partir de los mosaicos de terreno de la vista 3D; líneas más cercanas al acercarse.
land.contours_layer.definition: While the layer is on, the browser asks the AWS Terrain Tiles (Terrarium encoding, the source of the 3D view's terrain; in Puerto Rico from USGS 3DEP) for the tiles in view up to zoom 15, decodes each pixel's height ((R x 256 + G + B / 256) - 32768 m) and traces the contour lines with marching squares. The interval is 100 m up to zoom 11, 50 m at 12, 20 m at 13 and 10 m from 14; every fifth line is thicker. Nothing is stored in the observatory's files.
land.contours_layer.method: js/terrain.js: marching squares on each 256 x 256 tile, the saddle cells split by the mean of their four corners; levels above 0 m only.
land.contours_layer.how_to_read: Lines close together mean steep ground; far apart, gentle ground. Read the thicker lines for the height in round numbers.
caveats: Lines are traced tile by tile, so a line can have a one-pixel gap where two tiles meet.
The terrain tiles are about 5 m at the closest zoom and are smoothed at the island's scale.

land.slope_layer.plain: A map of how steep the ground is, darker for steeper, from the USGS 10 m elevation model. A slider shows only the land at or above a slope.
land.slope_layer.plain_es: Un mapa de cuán empinado es el terreno, más oscuro mientras más empinado, a partir del modelo de elevación de 10 m del USGS. Un control deslizante muestra solo el terreno con una pendiente dada o más.
land.slope_layer.definition: slope_surface.png is an indexed Web Mercator image of 3730 x 1241 pixels of about 59 m: each pixel is the mean slope of the 10 m cells of one block of slope.py, on a fixed scale of 64 steps from 0% to 60% (steeper is drawn as 60%), transparent over the sea. slope_surface.json gives its corners, size and scale. The 2D map lays it at 75% opacity under the landslide and soil layers; the legend's slider leaves out the steps below a chosen slope, and a click on the map gives the slope of the block under the point.
land.slope_layer.method: slope.py reads the USGS 3DEP 1/3 arc-second elevation tiles over Puerto Rico in windows of 0.1 degree (raster.py) and computes the slope of every 10 m cell by Horn's method, with the cell's size in metres at its latitude, as rise over run x 100; a cell next to one with no height has no slope. The cells are counted in blocks of 6 x 6 (about 60 m); a block belongs to the barrio that holds its centre (the nearest within 100 m off the coast), and blocks in no barrio (the sea) are left out. Municipios and Puerto Rico pool their barrios' cells. Checks at every build: Puerto Rico's share steeper than 30% between 15% and 55%; Jayuya, Orocovis and Barranquitas steeper than Puerto Rico; Cataño with less than 5% of its land steeper than 15%; the cells counted cover 97% to 110% of the barrios' Census land area.
land.slope_layer.how_to_read: Pale is flat, dark brown is steep. Move the slider to 15% or 30% to see only the land steeper than that. The shares by barrio are in Explore.
caveats: Heights are of the bare ground at about 10 m: cuts, retaining walls and terraces narrower than a cell are smoothed out, and a road on a bridge reads the ground below.
Each pixel is the mean of a block of about 60 m, so a narrow steep bank inside a flatter block looks gentler than it is.
land.slope_layer.geography: Puerto Rico, Vieques and Culebra (Mona, Monito and Desecheo are not drawn)

environment.mangrove_km2.plain: How much mangrove forest each municipio has.
environment.mangrove_km2.plain_es: Cuánto bosque de mangle tiene cada municipio.
environment.mangrove_km2.definition: The area of the inventory's estuarine intertidal forested and scrub-shrub wetlands with broad-leaved evergreen plants (codes E2FO3 and E2SS3), which in Puerto Rico are mangroves, in square kilometres.
environment.mangrove_km2.method: environment_series.py reads the inventory's polygons of Puerto Rico from its map service and keeps the three wetland types (estuarine and marine wetland, freshwater emergent, freshwater forested and shrub). Each polygon is split among the municipal boundaries in metres (NAD83 Puerto Rico); the part beyond the drawn coast goes to the municipio with the largest share. Mangroves are the polygons coded E2FO3 or E2SS3.
environment.mangrove_km2.how_to_read: 94.99 km² for Puerto Rico; the most in Loíza 13.8 km², Ceiba 9.4 km², Río Grande 7.1 km².
caveats: Mapped from photographs of 1983, before later losses and recovery (Hurricane María among them).
environment.mangrove_km2.source_detail: USFWS National Wetlands Inventory map service, layer Wetlands: ATTRIBUTE, WETLAND_TYPE and the outline; photo years from the Data_Source service

environment.wetland_pct.definition: Wetland area divided by the municipio's land area (Census), in percent.
environment.wetland_pct.method: environment_series.py reads the inventory's polygons of Puerto Rico from its map service and keeps the three wetland types (estuarine and marine wetland, freshwater emergent, freshwater forested and shrub). Each polygon is split among the municipal boundaries in metres (NAD83 Puerto Rico); the part beyond the drawn coast goes to the municipio with the largest share. Mangroves are the polygons coded E2FO3 or E2SS3.
environment.wetland_pct.how_to_read: 5.51% for Puerto Rico; the highest in Loíza 71.6%, Cataño 44.8%, Toa Baja 35.5%.
caveats: Coastal wetlands can lie partly on what the Census counts as water, so a small coastal municipio's share can be high.
Almost all of the wetland area was mapped from photographs of 1983.

environment.wetland_km2.how_to_read: 488.27 km² for Puerto Rico; the most in Lajas 38.5 km², Loíza 35.9 km², Cabo Rojo 24.8 km².
caveats: Almost all of the wetland area was mapped from aerial photographs of 1983: wetlands filled or restored since then are not shown.
Areas are worked out from the inventory's outlines and can differ from official acreages.

land.calificacion.plain: The observatory does not publish zoning districts (Calificación). The Junta de Planificación's map service was not available when the 2026-10 snapshot was built. A zoning layer is planned; no date is set.
land.calificacion.plain_es: El observatorio no publica los distritos de calificación. El servicio de mapas de la Junta de Planificación no estaba disponible cuando se preparó el corte de datos de 2026-10. Hay planes para una capa de calificación, pero no tiene fecha.
land.calificacion.definition: Calificación is the zoning district assigned to land under the Reglamento Conjunto (the joint planning regulation), published by the Junta de Planificación de Puerto Rico in its Mapa Interactivo de Puerto Rico (MIPR). The Junta's map service returned an error when the 2026-10 snapshot was built (the build file meta.json records the failed request; see data.build_landuse), so no zoning data are in the observatory. None of the observatory's data files holds this layer.
land.calificacion.method: At each build the observatory asks the MIPR service for its list of layers. Even when the service answers, the observatory does not yet download or publish the zoning layer. The 2D map and the Housing page show a note that zoning is pending.
land.calificacion.how_to_read: Do not read the Plan de Uso de Terrenos class (for example Suelo Urbano) as the zoning of a lot. The Plan is a broad classification; zoning is a separate layer that the observatory does not yet show.
caveats: Nothing in the observatory tells what may be built on a given lot. Check the Junta de Planificación or the municipality for zoning.
The Junta's service returned an error when the 2026-10 snapshot was built. Even if it answers later, the observatory does not publish the layer until a later snapshot adds it.
